questions.def: 'Were' signals a hypothetical situation; hence, 'would call'.
questions.question: Were he to need help, he ___ me.

questions.def: Past unreal conditional uses 'would have + past participle'.
questions.question: Had I known, I ___ differently.

questions.def: 'Should' requires the base form of the verb: 'Should you need'.
questions.question: Should you needed anything, do not hesitate to ask.

questions.def: 'Were I to be' is the correct formal conditional form.
questions.question: Were I to ___ you, I'd accept the offer.

questions.def: Past unreal conditional: 'would have' + past participle.
questions.question: Had they arrived earlier, they ___ the train.

questions.def: 'Should' conditional usually takes 'will' in the result clause.
questions.question: Should it rain, we ___ inside.

questions.def: 'Had' requires the past participle form: 'Had I known'.
questions.question: Had I knew about the party, I would have gone.

questions.def: Past perfect is needed after 'Had' for the unreal past.
questions.question: Had she ___ the truth, she would have reacted differently.

questions.def: 'Were' implies a hypothetical situation, using 'would'.
questions.question: Were he rich, he ___ a big house.

questions.def: 'Should' often introduces a request. 'Let me know' is appropriate.
questions.question: Should you need anything, ___.

questions.def: Needs 'would have' + past participle: 'would have avoided'.
questions.question: Had they listened, they would avoided the problem.

questions.def: 'Had' requires the past participle form of the verb.
questions.question: Had we ___ earlier, we wouldn't have missed the start.

questions.def: 'Were' implies a hypothetical situation; use 'would + verb'.
questions.question: Were it not raining, we ___ to the beach.

questions.def: 'Should' conditional often uses an imperative in the result.
questions.question: Should you decide to come, ___ us a call.

questions.def: Unreal past conditional requires 'would have' not 'will have'.
questions.question: Had I been there, I will have helped.

questions.def: 'Had' requires the past participle of the verb, 'studied'.
questions.question: Had she ___ harder, she would have passed the exam.

questions.def: 'Were' indicates a hypothetical situation; use 'would + verb'.
questions.question: Were she to ask, I ___ her the truth.

questions.def: 'Should' conditional with an imperative 'give' in the main clause.
questions.question: Should you see him, ___ him my regards.

questions.def: Past unreal conditional: 'wouldn't have' not 'won't have'.
questions.question: Had they understood, they won't have made that mistake.

questions.def: 'Had' requires the past participle of the verb, 'listened'.
questions.question: Had you ___ to me, you wouldn't be in this mess.

questions.def: 'Were' implies a hypothetical situation; use 'would'.
questions.question: Were I to win the lottery, I ___ travel the world.

questions.def: Object pronoun 'him' is needed after 'tell'.
questions.question: Should he call, tell ___ I'm busy.

questions.def: Needs 'would have' + past participle: 'would have told'.
questions.question: Had she knew the answer, she would told us immediately.

questions.def: 'Were I to do' is the correct formal conditional form.
questions.question: Were I to ___ it again, I'd do it differently.

questions.def: Third conditional: 'would have' + past participle.
questions.question: Had I known you were coming, I ___ dinner.

questions.def: Use 'please' to make the request polite.
questions.question: Should you see my keys, ___ let me know.

questions.def: Use the base form: 'say so'.
questions.question: Should you want to leave, just said so I will understand.

questions.def: Past participle is needed after 'Had'.
questions.question: Had I ___ him, he would have failed.

questions.def: 'Were' implies a hypothetical situation, 'could' expresses ability.
questions.question: Were she older, she ___ drive.

questions.def: 'Should' conditional often uses an imperative in the result.
questions.question: Should you change your mind, ___ me.
